findings: Fresh pilot cleanup now requires the complete frozen campaign/numerical/input identity, all three full pilot audits, exact raw/H200 original hashes, successful dispatch/startup/launch/child provenance, completed bounded entry/controller guards and full remaining storage.

The immutable pre-deletion review binds all original files and audits. The existing600s/4GiB/8GiB executor receives hard-coded authorization/revalidation callbacks; every removal rechecks STOP, frozen context, protected metadata and dispatch guards. Only the six audited pilot weights enter the manifest.

After deletion, the controller verifies the full execution journal/guard/receipt chain, protected evidence and complete future storage, then publishes completion only after its bounded controller guard finishes. Failures remain permanent, including failures after weights were already removed.

A new read-only pre-quality verifier reconstructs the exact manifest from preserved pre-deletion records and verifies the complete chain, current protected files, dispatch provenance, controller guard and current storage. It does not reload deleted pilot tensors or authorize a quality worker.

Initial integration tests exposed a synthetic fixture rewriting an existing immutable request with different JSON formatting and restoring stale nominal process storage totals. Production verification correctly rejected this; fixture requests now retain exact bytes and launch limits, with all failed logs preserved.

The next test run showed that its mocked frozen gate hid STOP, allowing the synthetic executor to finish all six removals before post-verification failed. The new controller now checks STOP directly in its per-removal frozen-context callback as well as requiring the real frozen gate. Final tests stop after exactly one removal and retain intent/deleted/failure evidence.

Successful synthetic cleanup removed exactly six disposable tiny checkpoint files, preserved every other pre-existing evidence hash, and passed verification after tensors were absent. Partial pilots, missing/altered audits or dispatches, extra weights, invalid guards, changed metadata, incomplete journals, recreated weights and post-cleanup storage failure are rejected.
limitations: The complete frozen campaign gate and training/process science are mocked in integration fixtures. The final309-test suite includes real temporary locks, guarded cleanup/journal execution, receipt-chain/storage logic and surrounding audit/dispatch/startup tests. This is not actual numerical, training, cache, MPS or model-quality evidence.
No research checkpoint was deleted. All removals were disposable synthetic bytes in temporary test directories; retained research checkpoints, failures and closed holdout remain untouched.

The new API has no CLI, plan freeze, retry, training, stage continuation or adoption action. Callers must inspect actual workers, hold both locks and use resource guards for read-only verification. Later LR/rank boundaries still need controller integration.

Quality/selection/cleanup-chain/inference orchestration, actual nine rank-policy numerical/input prerequisites and measured pilots remain unresolved. The failed combined CPU fixture remains closed and no MPS launch occurred.

Deleted real pilot tensors would no longer be reloadable or tensor-auditable; future acceptance relies on preserved pre-deletion audits and verified execution receipts. Actual full-panel storage remains near the threshold and must be rechecked before any real transition.
